correctness.rationale: The multiprojective equations are invariant under the diagonal change-of-basis torus. A generic one-parameter subgroup separates the matrix-coordinate weights in every projective factor, so every fixed point is a tuple of matrix units. Two consecutive matrix units compose nontrivially exactly when the intermediate target and source indices coincide. Thus the first arrow contributes d_0 d_1 choices and each later arrow contributes (d_{i-1}-1)d_i choices, giving d_0 d_n prod_i d_i(d_i-1). Euler localization applies to arbitrary projective complex algebraic varieties, including reducible and singular ones. The packaged checker independently enumerates fixed coordinate tuples on a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: The multiprojective variety of complexes is a classical algebraic parameter space explicitly used in the literature, and its affine counterpart is a prototypical singular moduli space. The theorem gives a closed topological invariant for arbitrary length and arbitrary dimension vector. The answer has a structural interpretation: each intermediate vector space contributes exactly d_i(d_i-1), or equivalently a relative Euler factor 1-1/d_i, recording the single forbidden index match between consecutive coordinate maps. It also detects the sharp emptiness boundary at any one-dimensional intermediate space. This is a natural all-family invariant of the exact multiprojective object, not a small numerical slice.
